_comment: Art that proves the game HUD is on screen, i.e. that we are actually in play.
WHAT THESE TEMPLATES CONTAIN IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME - they are cut down to the statue frames
and NOTHING else. They used to include a band of the game world showing above the orbs, plus
the live life/mana readout and a slice of the orb liquid. In a bright room that band happens
to correlate; in an unlit catacomb it is black, and since TM_CCOEFF_NORMED normalises over the
whole patch, a quarter of the template being scenery dragged the score to 0.56 and the pipeline
announced NOT IN GAME with the HUD in plain view. See Error_history.txt #44 before recutting:
a reference must contain only pixels that CANNOT change.
TWO references, on OPPOSITE CORNERS, and EITHER ONE is enough, because occlusion during play
is normal and local - a tooltip, a panel, a spell effect covers one part of the screen. A
looser threshold would not do instead: it would trade away the thing that stops a lobby
matching. Note the two must fail INDEPENDENTLY for that to hold, which is exactly what the
old templates got wrong - both included game world, so one dark room took out both at once.
Measured at CAPTURE_SCALE 0.3 with these templates (tests/test_presence.py asserts the margin):
in game, unlit catacomb        right 0.931   left 0.867
in game, tooltip over an orb   right 0.897   left 0.937
lobby                          right 0.433   left 0.263
lobby with name-clash dialog   right 0.431   left 0.275
region and search_region are fractions of the ANCHOR WINDOW (see window_region.py), so
they survive the game being windowed, moved or resized. source_size stays 1920x1080 - it is
the resolution the art was cut AT, not the template's own size, so cropping does not touch it.
